text:
Thank you for taking this survey! Your participation will help us learn more about how people understand the world around them.
 
 
Over the next several minutes, you will see a number of short videos, each showing a simple scene. In each scene there will be a pink sphere and a gray cannonball, above a field of grass, with a hole in it. 
 
Please look at each scene carefully. Press play on the video to see the simulation begin. You will see only the first second of each simulation, but we want you to think about what would happen if the simulation kept going. Watch the simulation as many times as you need to understand what is going on in the scene.
 
For each scene, you will be asked to answer a question about what would happen if the simulation kept going. In some cases, you might also be asked about what would happen if a particular outcome occurred. Below the scene will be a slider, from which you can select a number from 0 - 100. Please use the slider to tell us how likely you think each question is, in percents. 

For example, if the question is, "How likely is the cannonball to end up in the hole?" and you set the slider to 99, that means you think there's a 99% chance the cannonball will end up in the hole — basically certain! If you set the slider to 1, that means you think there's only a 1% chance the cannonball will end up in the hole, which means you think it's pretty much impossible. If you set the slider to 50, that means you think it's 50-50 that the cannonball will end up in the hole, even odds, like flipping a coin.

This is an example of what the scenes look like, and how the objects act. Please press play to view. This is an example of what a full simulation looks like. 
 
On the next few pages, you will see a few more examples. Please watch them each a few times so that you know how the simulations work.

Please press play to view. This is a short clip, similar to what you will see in the body of the survey. As you can see, you can get a pretty good idea of what will happen next, but you still have to think a little to predict what you think is likely to happen next.

Please press play to view. This is another example of a full simulation.
 
If balls go off the side of the screen, as they do here, you can assume they end up on the grass.

feedback: Correct ranges: red chip greater than 22% and less than 28%; blue chip greater than 72% and less than 78%.
